says: The HUD is bright. Something in it is near white.
why: All four references clear it, from 0.662 to 0.940. A HUD dimmer than the world it sits on is a HUD the player has to hunt for.

says: HUD elements carry strong colour, not grey.
why: All four run 0.735 to 1.000. A child finds a red bar and a gold number. Grey chrome is an adult convention and disappears over a green field.

says: The HUD is made of few large shapes, never fine detail.
why: All four sit between 0.028 and 0.057, a tight agreement across four unrelated games. Fine detail at arm length on a phone is noise, and noise over a moving world is worse.

says: Anything a player taps is at least 11% of the screen short edge.
why: The platform minimum touch target is 44 pt on a screen 390 pt wide, which is 11.3%. A child panicking in a horde is less accurate than an adult, not more, so 11% is a floor and not a target. On a 1080 px short edge that is 120 px.

says: The HUD says things with icons and numbers, never sentences.
why: The game is for children, some of whom cannot read, and for a player whose eyes must return to the cat inside a second.

says: Every HUD element stays readable over the brightest part of the arena.
why: The world direction is a bright warm day. A HUD designed against a dark mock-up will vanish over lit grass, and this is only settled by looking at both together.
